notes.text: HPE Networking has released patches for the HPE Networking Wireless Operating Systems (AOS-8 and AOS-10) for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways, and Access Points that address multiple security vulnerabilities.
notes.title: Summary

notes.text:
HPE Networking 
  - Mobility Conductors 
  - Mobility Controllers
  - Mobility Gateways (Managed by HPE Networking Central)
  - AOS-10 Access Points (AOS-AP)
  - AOS-8 Instant Access Points (AOS-IAP)

Affected Software Version(s):
  - AOS-10.8.x.x: 10.8.1.1 and below
  - AOS-10.7.x.x: 10.7.2.6 and below
  - AOS-10.4.x.x: 10.4.1.13 and below
  - AOS-8.13.x.x: 8.13.3.0 and below
  - AOS-8.10.x.x: 8.10.0.23 and below
notes.title: Affected Products

notes.text: Any other HPE Networking products and software versions not specifically listed above are not affected by these vulnerabilities.
notes.title: Unaffected Products

notes.text: These vulnerabilities were generally discovered by internal security research at HPE Networking. document.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in HPE Networking Wireless Operating Systems (AOS-8 and AOS-10) for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways, and Access Points.

notes.text: Authentication bypass vulnerabilities in the affected interface of AOS-10 could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary commands on the underlying host if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system.

notes.title: Internal Reference

remediations.details:
Upgrade HPE Networking Wireless Operating Systems (AOS-10) for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways, and Access Points to one of the following versions (as applicable) to resolve the vulnerabilities described in the details section:
  - AOS-10.8.x.x: 10.8.1.2 and above
  - AOS-10.7.x.x: 10.7.2.7 and above
  - AOS-10.4.x.x: 10.4.1.14 and above

https://networkingsupport.hpe.com/downloads;fileTypes=SOFTWARE

To minimize the likelihood of an attacker exploiting these vulnerabilities, HPE Networking recommends that the CLI and web-based management interfaces be restricted to a dedicated layer 2 segment/VLAN and/or controlled by firewall policies at layer 3 and above along with accounting controls for tracking and logging user activities and resource usage.
